title: Evaluate card stand strength and finish
goal: I can check my actual stand, make a useful change and explain the result.
success: I can use the agreed one-card test safely and record what happened.
I can check strength and finish as different features.
I can make one approved improvement and log why it helps, then recheck.
purpose: Invented client Sam needs one lightweight paper prompt card, 80 mm wide and 60 mm high, upright and readable on a level table. The whole stand, including its channel, should fit a 160 mm wide by 120 mm deep table area. It should hold the card for 30 seconds with hands away. The card should lift out by hand. Plan safe smooth edges and no loose sharp parts. These are invented design targets, not standards.
continuity: Retrieve the actual approved design, build plan, Week 2 mock-up or Week 3 made item and change log. The default triangular body base is 120 mm by 80 mm; the U channel projects beyond the front. Use the actual approved revised plan if it differs. A missing or unfinished item stays honestly marked. Do not relabel an adult model as pupil work.
baseline_steps: Put tools down and return them as agreed. The adult checks actual edges, folds, joins, channel, table and safe support. Damaged or suspect edges are handled by the adult. Any actual approved adhesive join must complete the full cure on its checked label before testing.
Use a clear level table. Place the stand in a 160 mm by 120 mm overall table area. Use one actual lightweight paper card 80 mm wide by 60 mm high. Put it centrally in the U channel against the slope.
After adult clearance, keep hands away and observe for 30 seconds. Record the actual count, time and result. Stop at the first slip, tilt, bow, loose join, damage, concern or adult stop signal.
Gently remove the card. Look at folds, joins and channel with the adult. Do not touch suspect edges. A planned test is not a result.

Agree one safe useful change linked to a real finding. Make it with approved support. Repeat the one-card test with the same card, position, table and 30-second target after adult clearance. Log the actual before and after. A new adhesive repair keeps the recheck pending until its full checked label cure.
strength_finish: Do the body and joins support the intended one-card load?
Watch for slip, tilt, bowing or a loose join during the cleared normal-use test.
Are edges, folds, tape and channel neatly made and safe?
Inspect safe smooth edges, neat folds, flat secure tape and an open aligned channel.
finish_checks: Safe smooth edges; ask the adult about any suspect edge.
Neat folds that keep the planned shape.
Paper tape lies flat and secure, without loose ends.
U channel is aligned and open, with its front stop up toward the card.
No loose bits or sharp parts.
Card message stays readable and the card lifts out by hand.
stretch_load: Optional Stretch comparison only: first pass the one-card baseline and ask the adult to clear the next stage. Use a second identical lightweight paper card, then a third, maximum three cards total. Each is 80 mm by 60 mm and made from the same lightweight paper; no added clips, lamination or weights. Observe for 30 seconds at each stage. Remove cards and inspect between stages. Stop at the first concern; never add another card after a stop. Keep card size and material, position, level table and timing the same. The purpose is still one card. This is a comparison, not a maximum load or safety claim.
safety: Use the intended one lightweight paper card first. A normal-use load test does not need a heavy weight or force.
The adult clears actual joins, edges, tool return, table and support before the test. Keep hands away while observing; no one steadies the stand.
Stop for slip, tilt, bowing, loose join, damage, concern or the adult signal. Remove the load safely as directed. Let the adult handle damaged or suspect parts.
No pushing, shaking, dropping, heavy objects or tests to failure. No hot glue, heated tools or power tools are used.
Any repair uses only the actual approved hand-tool method and support. Close scissors and put them down before speaking or pausing. Ask before a new cut or join.
After a change, return to one card first. Record a stopped or unperformed test honestly. Do not add another card to see what happens after a warning.

An actual approved adhesive join must complete its full label cure before testing. The adult checks the actual instructions; never guess a cure time. A new adhesive repair keeps the recheck pending until full cure. The default uses cold paper tape.
model_change: Adult model only: Before the test, I saw a loose paper-tape end near the channel. The adult approved replacing that tape neatly without blocking the opening. I recorded the change as a finish improvement. I then used the same one-card test and wrote what actually happened. This account gives a method, not a pupil result or a guaranteed improvement.
fallback: With no actual stand or safe test space, use the model brief and spoken checks. Point, speak or sign a strength check, a finish check and a proposed improvement with a reason. Rehearse the stop routine with empty hands. An adult may scribe exact confirmed words. Label this model evaluation or planning. Actual load testing, physical improvement and the recheck stay pending unless performed.
careers: Product testers use a fair normal-use check and record limits. Makers use those findings to improve joins, handling and finish before the product is used.

stages.name: Arrival
stages.title: Find the real stand and record
pupil: Find your actual design, item and change log.
Tell the adult what is finished or still pending.
Wait for the work and test area to be cleared.
stages.teacher: Retrieve actual approved records and work. Keep a Week 2 mock-up labelled as a mock-up, and an adult model labelled as a model. Read the one-card purpose. Check actual joins, edges, table clearance, tool return and support before any handling or test. If the item is missing, use the model evaluation route without inventing earlier making. Use the last minute for a calm settling pause.
stages.check: Ask what the intended load is. Expect one actual lightweight paper card, 80 mm by 60 mm, not a real device, heavy object or maximum-load challenge.

stages.name: Starter
stages.title: Strength or finish
pupil: Strength is support under the intended load.
Finish is the quality of edges, folds and joins.
One check can reveal a useful next step.
stages.teacher: Compare strength with finish using the two-row card. A neat tape surface alone does not prove the stand holds the card. A standing card alone does not prove every edge is safe. Use actual observations only after clearance. Read aloud or point to one check at a time.
stages.check: Ask which check belongs to strength: card stays supported during the timed test, or tape lies flat. Expect the first. Tape quality is a finish check, though joins can affect strength too.

stages.name: I do
stages.title: Model a safe normal-use test
pupil: Watch the adult clear the stand and level table.
One card sits in the U channel. Hands away for 30 seconds.
Stop at the first concern; do not test to failure.
stages.teacher: Demonstrate on an adult teaching stand or narrate a clearly labelled model if none is available. Put tools down and inspect the work. Place one 80 by 60 mm paper card centrally in the channel against the slope. Observe hands away for 30 seconds only if cleared. Show how to record actual time and result. Stop immediately if a concern appears; do not manufacture a fault. Remove the card and inspect folds, joins and channel. Model one observation, then fade the next question to the pupil.
stages.check: Ask for one stop sign and the safe response. Expect slip, tilt, bowing, loose join, damage, concern or adult signal; stop and follow the adult, without adding load.

stages.name: We do
stages.title: Our first test and finish check
pupil: Use the cleared one-card test with support.
Record the actual card count, time and what happened.
Check edges, folds, tape and channel.
stages.teacher: Guide a baseline one-card test only after the actual item and route are cleared. One pupil may direct safe adult handling; record the roles. Keep card position central, table level and timing target 30 seconds. Remove and inspect. Use the finish list and record a real finding or that a feature was met. Do not call an adult-model demonstration pupil testing. Plan in any language and confirm scribed words.
stages.check: Check that the entry gives an actual observation, not a copied target. If the stand needs a safety repair before any test, record baseline test stopped or not performed and why. Do not invent a before result.

stages.name: We do 2
stages.title: Should the next card be added
pupil: The stand tilts during the one-card test.
Should you add another card to test its strength?
Choose a safe response and explain why.
stages.teacher: Hinge answer is no. Stop at the first concern, remove the load as the adult directs and inspect before any approved change. Never add load after a stop. Parallel check: after a repair, should you start with three cards? No. Recheck with one intended card first, after adult clearance. If either response is missed, rehearse tools down, stop, ask and one-card recheck before practical work resumes.
stages.check: Move on when the pupil explains the stop sign, adult check and one-card restart. A quiz answer does not clear the actual item or optional comparison.

stages.name: Independent
stages.title: Improve one feature and recheck
pupil: Choose one real strength or finish finding.
Make one approved useful change with the agreed support.
Repeat the same one-card check and log the actual result.
stages.teacher: Keep approved supervision; independent is the timetable stage, not tool permission. Agree one useful safe improvement linked to a real finding, such as a neater secure tape end or corrected channel alignment. Do not deliberately weaken work to make a change. After repair, the adult clears the item and the same one-card test comes first. Log before, change, why, after result and support. If no safe improvement is suitable, keep the next step pending. Optional Stretch extra-card comparison is only after a successful baseline and separate adult clearance, maximum three identical paper cards total, with 30 seconds and removal/inspection between stages. It is never required. A new adhesive repair keeps the recheck pending until the full cure required by the actual checked label. Do not guess a time.
stages.check: Check real improvement and recheck evidence. If only a proposal was made or the test was not completed, label it accordingly. A stopped test is useful evidence and does not require a forced pass.

stages.name: Review
stages.title: Explain strength finish and change
pupil: Put tools down and return them as agreed.
Compare before and after under the same conditions.
State a remaining gap or honest next step.
stages.teacher: Count and return any repair tools before review. Let the pupil explain one strength observation and one finish finding, privately if preferred. Compare the same one-card conditions before and after. A stopped baseline or missing recheck stays explicit. Confirm roles and exact pupil words. Extra-card counts show only this comparison, not a universal capacity. Use the last minute to store the item and log together.
stages.check: Ask what changed and why, what the actual recheck shows and what remains uncertain. Do not mark strength or finish as passed from a model picture or an unperformed test.

stages.name: Exit
stages.title: My real test and improvement record
pupil: My strength check showed ___.
My finish finding was ___. I changed ___ because ___.
The recheck showed ___ / stays pending because ___.
stages.teacher: Retain the actual dated evaluation, finish list, improvement log, support and evidence location for the closing review next week. Object-only sketches or a private school-approved object photo may support the record; no people or identifiers and no public upload. A presentation of planning is not a practical test.
stages.check: Evidence records actual strength and finish checks, a real approved improvement and its reason, the actual recheck or honest gap, and support. The lesson does not certify the unit award or a maximum load.

Supported: Use one check at a time with the adult. Point to the real stand or name the model route.
Direct the cleared one-card test and say what happened; record the true roles.
Point to one finish finding. Choose an approved useful improvement and explain why.
Confirm the before and after record. Keep any unperformed action pending.
Standard: Use the actual one-card baseline with the agreed support and stop rules.
Record strength and finish findings separately.
Make one approved improvement linked to a real finding.
Repeat the same one-card check and log actual count, time, result, support and next step.
Stretch: Finish the core one-card test, finish check and real change log first.
Say why the before and after checks are fair. Say what they do not prove.
First pass the one-card check. Ask the adult before each extra card. Try two then three matching paper cards at most.
Use 30 seconds each. Remove all cards and inspect between stages. Stop at the first concern. This is a comparison, not maximum capacity.

vocabulary: How well the stand and joins support the intended load.
The quality of edges, folds, tape and other final details.
What the stand carries. Our intended load is one paper card.
A check that keeps the same conditions when comparing a change.
Something you really observed or measured.
A useful change linked to a real finding and a reason.

adaptations.Cognition and Learning: Read one check at a time. Use strength and finish as two clear groups. Model observation, change, reason and recheck, then fade to sentence starts. Keep actual results separate from target numbers.
adaptations.Communication and Interaction: Offer pointing, speech, signing and pupil-directed adult handling. Give thinking time. Read back any scribed finding so the pupil can correct it. Keep the actual roles visible.
adaptations.SEMH: Use private feedback and an optional calm pause. A pause starts with tools down and work safe. Treat a stopped test as information, not a personal failure. No forced public display or personal disclosure.
adaptations.Sensory and Physical: Check seating, grip and line of sight. Use a large view, adult handling directed by the pupil or a no-touch model evaluation. Do not force contact with suspect edges or unstable work. Record practical actions still pending.
adaptations.Literacy and Numeracy: Keep one-card count and actual seconds in separate fields. Read 80 mm by 60 mm as card size. Use before and after sentence starts. Planned 30 seconds is not an actual timing unless observed.
adaptations.EAL: Plan in any language. Pair strength, finish, load and stop with the actual part or a gesture. Rehearse short observation and reason phrases. Preserve meaning through confirmed scribing.
